title: How to choose a wedding venue: the complete guide
seo_title: How to choose a wedding venue: the complete guide
dek: Find the perfect setting for your celebration with this expert guide on budgets, locations and the practical details of how to choose a wedding venue.
body:
Selecting where you will celebrate your marriage is the most significant decision in your planning process. This choice dictates your date, your guest list and the overall atmosphere of the celebration, making it essential to understand how to choose a wedding venue that aligns with your vision and your finances. By focusing on your priorities early, you can find a space that serves as a beautiful backdrop for your ceremony and reception.

## Establishing your budget and guest list

Your budget and guest list are the two most influential factors in determining how to choose a wedding venue. Because venue hire and catering typically account for 51% of total wedding spending, according to Which? experts, these figures must be settled before you begin your search.

### Defining your financial boundaries
Setting a strict budget early helps prevent the overspending that affects more than half of newly married couples, according to a survey by insurance provider Protectivity. While even smaller celebrations often cost between £5,000 to £10,000, Savills research shows that 25% of couples spend over £26,000 on their wedding.

To manage these costs, Roko recommends creating a detailed spreadsheet to track every expense as plans develop. You can find a breakdown of how these figures compare to national averages in Roko's guide to [weddings by the numbers](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show).

### The relationship between guests and cost
Your guest count dictates the size of the venue you require and the volume of food and drink needed. Savills reports that the average cost per guest has risen to £272, even as guest numbers have generally fallen.

To find your price per head, take your total venue and catering budget and divide it by your desired guest count. This figure will be your primary filter when you [browse wedding vendors](/wedding-vendors) on Roko.

| Wedding Scale | Estimated Total Budget |
| :--- | :--- |
| Small and intimate | £5,000 to £10,000 |
| Mid-range | £10,000 to £26,000 |
| Premium and luxury | Over £26,000 |

If your preferred venue exceeds your price per head, you face a trade-off: you must either reduce your guest list or find savings in other categories. Photography and videography usually account for 10% of costs, while decor and entertainment take up roughly 7%.

Choosing a smaller guest list is one of the most effective ways to control your total spend. This approach allows you to prioritise quality over quantity, perhaps choosing a more prestigious venue that would be unaffordable for a larger group. Conversely, if a large guest list is non-negotiable, you may need to look at unconventional locations, such as local pubs or community spaces, which can often cut hire fees in half or offer the space for nothing if you guarantee a minimum spend at the bar.

## Defining your wedding style and atmosphere

The atmosphere of your celebration is dictated by the architectural character and setting of your venue. According to Savills research, modern couples are moving away from rigid, package-led formats in favour of celebrations that feel highly personalised and authentic. When deciding how to choose a wedding venue, you should first determine which aesthetic aligns with the story you want to tell.

### Stylish and formal
For a sophisticated, urban atmosphere, formal wedding venues and luxury hotels provide a polished backdrop. In Dubai, the Raffles hotel offers an Egyptian aesthetic with an opulent ballroom featuring Swarovski chandeliers. Similarly, the St. Regis Downtown Dubai provides a prestigious setting with views of the Dubai Water Canal and the city skyline. These locations suit couples who want a mature, high-quality environment that works well with urban photography. Kokoro Switch suggests these venues are ideal for those who have taken pre-wedding photos in popular city locations and want to maintain that refined, urban feel.

### Elegant and classical
If you prefer a softer, more graceful world view, an elegant style pairs well with classical hotels and refined floral decorations. Locations like the Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri in Abu Dhabi combine Arabian charm with coastal views of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. This style is often chosen by those who have selected traditional attire or formal dresses and want a glamorous reception. Kokoro Switch research indicates that this aesthetic is particularly effective for couples who want to highlight the refined beauty of their chosen attire and a sophisticated world view.

### Natural and simple
For a more relaxed or at-home feeling, garden and restaurant settings offer an unadorned, natural atmosphere. Savills research found that 31% of couples believe an outside space is what sets their chosen venue apart from others. This might involve a quiet alfresco gathering in gardens, such as those at Raffles Dubai, or a ceremony on a stunning beachfront. At the One&Only Royal Mirage in Dubai, the Oval Lawn provides a garden setting with palm trees for private ceremonies of up to 250 guests.

### Experience-led and immersive
A growing trend in the industry is the move towards destination-style venues that support two-day or weekend-long celebrations. Savills notes that demand for these immersive experiences is rising as couples seek more time with their guests. This approach allows for a variety of atmospheres within one booking. For instance, JA The Resort in Dubai is known for hosting multi-day Indian weddings, tailoring celebrations around traditional events. This could include a grand ballroom reception followed by a rooftop soirée or a private garden gathering.

When researching styles, remember that 82% of couples use social media to find inspiration, and 66% value seeing imagery of real weddings in the spaces they are considering. You can [browse wedding vendors](/wedding-vendors) on Roko to see how different styles look in practice before you visit in person. For more ways to achieve a high-end look regardless of your choice, read Roko's guide on [luxury wedding ideas for every budget](/journal/luxury-wedding-ideas-for-every-budget).

## How to choose a wedding venue for your preferred date

The timing of your celebration is one of the most influential factors in determining availability and cost. When you consider how to choose a wedding venue, you must balance your ideal season with the reality of local demand and the premium prices often attached to specific dates. Focusing on these timing strategies early allows you to secure a location that fits both your vision and your timeline.

### Seasonality and peak periods
Demand for dates varies significantly by region and climate. In the UK, Savills research shows that 40% of 2025 wedding bookings fell within the peak period of May to August, an increase from 33% in 2024. August was the most popular month, accounting for 17% of celebrations, followed by May at 13% and September at 12%. The most popular individual date in the UK for 2025 was 15 September.

In Australia, the pattern reflects a preference for milder weather in autumn and spring. Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics show that higher numbers of marriages occur in these seasons, while winter and holiday periods like Christmas and Easter see lower volumes. The most popular date in Australia for 2025 was 25 October, followed by 22 November and 1 November. Other highly sought-after dates included 5 April and 18 October.

### The impact of the day of the week
Saturday remains the most common choice for weddings globally. In Australia, over 52,000 marriages took place on a Saturday in 2025, and 45 of the top 50 most popular dates fell on this day. Friday is the second most popular option, with just over 21,000 Australian marriages in 2025. The most popular Friday for that year was 10 October, which ranked as the 33rd most popular date overall.

Because of this high demand for weekends, many couples are looking at midweek options to manage costs or secure a specific location. Savills notes that budget sensitivity is contributing to growth in midweek and off-peak bookings. You can find further context on these trends in Roko's guide to [weddings by the numbers](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show).

### Timing strategies
Competition for premium dates is intense, with 2026 and 2027 bookings already tracking ahead of previous years. Savills reports that 4 in 5 couples book their venue within a month of their first contact. When you are ready to visit a space, it is useful to have a list of [questions to ask a wedding venue](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) regarding their specific date availability. If your heart is set on a popular month, you may need to book significantly further in advance or consider a Friday or Sunday to increase your chances of success. You can browse [wedding vendors](/wedding-vendors) on Roko to compare availability and styles for your chosen timeframe.

## Choosing the right location and venue type

The venue type you select is the primary factor in how to choose a wedding venue that fits your logistical needs. Different settings offer varying levels of service, from all-inclusive hotel packages to the flexibility of a rural barn or a local pub. According to Roko's analysis of market trends, 51% of wedding spending typically goes towards venue hire and catering, so the architectural style and location of your choice will heavily influence your remaining budget.

### Luxury hotels and integrated resorts

Hotels are often the preferred choice for those seeking a smooth, integrated experience. They provide on-site accommodation, professional event teams, and established catering. In markets like Dubai, luxury hotels often cater to multi-day celebrations. For instance, JA The Resort specialises in Indian weddings that require several days of traditional events, while the St. Regis Downtown Dubai offers ballrooms for up to 350 guests with a minimum spend starting from Dh350 per person as of 2026.

Hotels also offer distinct aesthetics, such as the Egyptian-inspired architecture of Raffles Dubai or the lakeside views of the Killyhevlin Lakeside Hotel in Northern Ireland, which recently underwent a £1.5 million investment to create its Loughview reception space. These venues are ideal if you want a high-quality, mature atmosphere with dedicated spaces for getting ready.

### Barns and rural escapes

Barns remain a significant trend in the wedding sector. Savills research indicates that many couples value "architecturally beautiful" spaces that are easy to decorate. These venues often appeal to those who want a more relaxed or rustic atmosphere. A key differentiator for these locations is the availability of outdoor areas; 2025 data shows that 31% of couples chose their venue specifically because of its outside space. 

While barns offer a beautiful backdrop, they may require more coordination if they do not provide in-house catering or furniture. You can browse wedding venues on Roko to compare those offering full-service packages against those that serve as a simple hire space.

### Unconventional and community spaces

For those prioritising cost control or a unique atmosphere, unconventional locations like pubs, restaurants, and village halls are increasingly popular. Which? experts suggest that hosting a reception in a local pub can significantly reduce hire fees, sometimes even resulting in a free space if you guarantee a minimum spend, such as £1,000 at the bar.

These spaces allow for creative freedom, such as hiring a local pizza van or organising a "bring your own bottle" (BYOB) reception to manage alcohol costs. While these options require more DIY effort, they can cut the traditional hire fee in half. If you are looking for ways to balance a premium feel with a smaller budget, Roko's guide to [luxury wedding ideas for every budget](/journal/luxury-wedding-ideas-for-every-budget) offers further inspiration on styling these alternative spaces.

## Understanding venue packages and inclusions

Venue pricing generally falls into two categories: per-head packages or bespoke hire fees. Savills research indicates that 72% of couples will not contact a venue unless clear pricing is available online, highlighting the importance of transparency from the start. When you evaluate how to choose a wedding venue, understanding exactly what is included in these figures is essential to avoid unexpected costs.

### All-inclusive packages
Many hotels and dedicated event spaces offer tiered packages that simplify the planning process by bundling essential services. In the UAE market, for example, the St. Regis Downtown Dubai offers a Love Package starting at Dh350 per person, which includes a buffet or sharing menu, a two-layer wedding cake, a tasting for three people, and valet parking. Their Adore Package, priced at Dh400 per person, adds bespoke linens and welcome mocktails.

Other venues include experiential elements to differentiate their offering. The Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri in Abu Dhabi provides packages starting at Dh290 per person that include a bridal spa treatment or a private photo shoot on a traditional Abra boat. These models provide a predictable cost per guest, which helps in managing a strict budget.

### Bespoke hire and minimum spend
Some venues opt for a hire fee combined with a minimum spend on food and beverages. At the One&Only Royal Mirage in Dubai, venue hire is set at Dh5,000 per day, but specific areas have significant minimum spend requirements. The Amphitheatre and Oval Lawn each require a minimum spend of Dh120,000, while the Peregrine Ballroom requires Dh80,000. Under this model, you pay for the exclusivity of the space and then customise your catering and drinks to reach the required threshold.

### External catering and hidden requirements
If you choose a venue that allows external caterers, there are often strict regulatory and quality standards to meet. According to Savills, venues must ensure that outside teams have the correct licensing, insurance, and sufficient staffing to manage both service and clearing. Before you commit, it is worth reviewing [questions to ask a wedding venue before you book](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) to ensure you understand their policy on external vendors.

### Essential inclusion checklist
When comparing quotes from [all event and wedding businesses](/wedding-vendors), check if the following are included or carry extra fees:
*   **AV and technical support**: Many packages include basic audio-visual equipment, but complex lighting or sound systems may cost more.
*   **Accommodation**: Check if a suite for the couple or discounted rates for guests are part of the deal.
*   **Service charges and taxes**: Ensure the quoted price is net or inclusive of all local taxes.
*   **Staffing**: Confirm there is adequate staff for the scale of your event, particularly for serving and clearing tables.

## Managing catering and beverage costs

Catering and venue hire typically account for 51% of total wedding spending. According to Savills research, the average cost per guest rose to £272 in 2025, making food and drink a primary area for potential savings. To keep your finances on track, calculate a price per head by dividing your total catering budget by your guest count. This figure serves as a benchmark when comparing formal sit-down meals against more informal alternatives.

### How to choose a wedding venue with flexible catering

While formal dining is a traditional choice, it is often the most expensive. Which? experts note that wedding catering costs average £5,406, with an additional £2,002 typically spent on evening snacks. Many couples are now moving away from rigid, package-led formats in favour of authentic experiences that offer better cost control.

Food trucks, such as local pizza vans, have gained popularity for their atmosphere and flexibility. Some vendors charge a set rate rather than a price per item, which can offer significant savings. If you choose a venue that allows external caterers, the venue will likely require them to meet specific standards for licensing, insurance and staffing. Other informal options that reduce costs include:

*   Buffets or hog roasts
*   Picnics for outdoor celebrations
*   Quotes from local cafes or independent restaurants rather than specialist wedding vendors

You can also reduce dessert costs by forgoing a specialist cake designer. Asking friends and family to bake their favourite cakes for a communal cake table can save hundreds of pounds. This approach creates a variety of choices for guests while staying well within a modest budget.

### Managing beverage costs and corkage

Providing alcohol is frequently one of the highest hidden expenses. A Bring Your Own Bottle (BYOB) approach can slash your total drinks bill by thousands of pounds, even after accounting for corkage fees.

| Beverage Type | Typical Corkage Fee |
| :--- | :--- |
| Wine | £15 per bottle |
| Champagne | £30 per bottle |

These fees cover the cost of the venue providing glassware and service. However, they are not always fixed. You should feel confident to haggle or specifically search for venues that do not charge for corkage. Buying bottles from wholesalers or during supermarket sales and paying the fee usually results in a lower total cost than using a venue's standard bar prices.

When you browse wedding venues on Roko, check whether they offer flexible catering policies or no-corkage options. For more ways to balance your preferences with your spending, read Roko's guide to [luxury wedding ideas for every budget](/journal/luxury-wedding-ideas-for-every-budget).

## Researching and visiting potential venues

Digital research is the primary starting point for the planning process globally. Savills research shows that 82% of couples use social media to research venues, and 66% value seeing high quality imagery of the physical spaces alongside photos of real weddings. When you are browsing, look for a dedicated space to get ready, as this is an increasingly popular requirement for couples.

Transparency regarding costs is a major factor in the early stages for couples in many markets. The same research indicates that 72% of couples will not contact a venue unless clear pricing is available online. This transparency allows you to effectively manage your budget and focus your energy on locations that are financially viable.

### Conducting a physical viewing
While digital galleries provide a sense of the aesthetic, a physical visit allows you to evaluate the atmosphere and practical flow of the event. Savills found that 31% of couples felt that an outside space was the feature that set their chosen venue apart from others. During your visit, assess how the transition between the ceremony, drinks reception and dinner will work, and check the quality of the on-site accommodation.

When touring a property, consider these key differentiators:
*   **Architecture and decor:** The most popular venues are often architecturally beautiful and easy to decorate.
*   **Package inclusions:** Confirm exactly what is provided in the hire fee.
*   **Photography potential:** Identify locations for portraits and group shots.
*   **Flexibility:** Ask about options for midweek or off-peak dates if you are looking for better value.

The timeline for making a decision is often shorter than many expect. Data shows that four in five couples book their venue within a month of their first contact. Because premium dates are in high demand, it is useful to have a prepared list of [questions to ask a wedding venue](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) before your tour begins.

If you are at the start of your search, you can browse wedding venues on Roko to filter by location and type. This helps you build a shortlist of businesses that match your specific style and guest count before you commit to travel for viewings.
